answer: Decentralized trust graphs mitigate Sybil attacks by bounding credit flow from established anchor nodes. At the dawn of each epoch, random walks detect sparse graph cuts, trapping forged identities on a topological island. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of cultivating scarce, genuine transaction histories with reputable peers. Despite a velvet trust curve that softens entry barriers, this mechanism inherently penalizes honest newcomer agents lacking social capital.
